title: How a housing boom became a crash

probes.question: What theory led to bundled subprime mortgages being valued so highly?
options: Interest rates would fall to zero

probes.question: True or false: the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers on 15 September 2008 is often considered the climax of the crisis.

image.alt: A white wooden sign reading FORECLOSURE in red letters in front of a suburban house.

panels.text: In 2006, after years of rising prices, US house prices peaked and mortgage delinquencies began to climb. It was the first sign the housing bubble was bursting.
Lending standards had grown lax. One-third of all mortgages in 2006 were subprime or no-documentation loans, which made up 17% of home purchases that year.
Bundled subprime mortgages were valued highly on the theory that housing prices would keep rising. Pay structures rewarded short-term deal flow over long-term value.
On 15 September 2008 Lehman Brothers, the fourth-largest US investment bank, went bankrupt. It is often considered the climax of the 2008 financial crisis.
